### The City of David
Author: Stuart Briscoe (One Year Devotions for Men)
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-men/the-city-of-david-one-year-devotions-for-men-january-16.html
Passage: Isaiah 29:13
Points:
- Isaiah refers to Jerusalem as Ariel, evoking an altar of sacrifice and blood.
- The altar pointed toward both God's judgment on sin and His promise of forgiveness.
- Persistently rejecting divine truth leaves people spiritually hardened and blind.
- Performing external religious rituals by rote cannot substitute for sincere faith.
- God's promised judgment arrived, but His redemptive blessing culminated in the Savior.

### Advent as Antidote to Christian Boredom
Author: Mike Pohlman
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/crosswalk-the-devotional-dec-4-2008-11596488.html
Passage: Isaiah 29:13-14
Points:
- People often take everyday wonders and human achievements for granted.
- Sin deadens our ability to marvel at God and the good news of the Gospel.
- Paying lip service to God while the heart is far away reduces faith to mere habit.
- Advent helps believers break out of monotony to contemplate Christ's incarnation.
- God overturns human complacency through the astounding wonders of His grace.

### Superstition
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/day-by-day-may-18-2009-11603661.html
Passage: Isaiah 29:13
Points:
- Superstitious practices grow out of fear and produce a false sense of security.
- People often rely on man-made traditions to feel safe instead of seeking God.
- Empty religious habits can lead believers into spiritual bondage.
- Sincerity in human ritual cannot replace authentic spiritual truth.
- True liberation comes only through Christ rather than outward religious forms.
